data.title: Brixton Metals Announces Closing of Non-Brokered Private Placement for Gross Proceeds of $1 Million
data.description:
Not for distribution to United States Newswire Services or for dissemination in the United States

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Brixton Metals Corporation (TSX- V: BBB, OTCQX: BBBXF) (the “Company” or “Brixton”) is pleased to announce that it has closed a non-brokered private placement offering (the “Offering”) of national flow-through shares in the capital of Brixton (the “FT Shares”) at a price of $0.68 per FT Share. In connection with closing the Offering, the Company issued 1,470,000 FT Shares for gross proceeds of $999,600.00.

The gross proceeds from the sale of FT Shares will be used to incur “Canadian exploration expenses” and “flow-through mining expenditures” as defined in the Income Tax Act (Canada). Exploration expenditures are mainly for exploration and drilling at the Company’s Langis Silver-Cobalt Project in Ontario.

All securities issued in connection with the Offering are subject to a hold period of four months and one day expiring on March 21, 2027 pursuant to applicable Canadian securities laws.

No finder’s fees were paid in connection with closing the Offering.

Option Grant

The Company’s Board has granted incentive stock options (each, an “Option”) to directors, officers, employees and consultants entitling the purchase of an aggregate of 1,840,000 common shares in the capital of the Company at a price of $0.465 for a period of 10 years. The Options will vest immediately with the exception of Options granted to investor relations personnel, which will vest in stages over 12 months from the date of grant with one-quarter of the Options granted to investor relations personnel vesting every three-month period following the date of grant in accordance with the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange.

About Brixton Metals Corporation

Brixton Metals is a Canadian exploration company focused on advancing its mining projects. Brixton wholly owns five exploration projects: the Langis and Hudson Bay silver Projects in Ontario; the Thorn copper-gold-silver-molybdenum Project in NW British Columbia; the Hog Heaven copper-silver-gold Project in NW Montana, USA, which is optioned to Ivanhoe Electric Inc.; and the Atlin Goldfields Project in northwest BC. Brixton holds an option to acquire a 100% interest in the silver-focused Silvergruvan Project in Sweden. Brixton Metals Corporation shares trade on the TSX-V under the ticker symbol BBB, and on the OTCQX under the ticker symbol BBBXF. For more information about Brixton, please visit our website at www.brixtonmetals.com.

data.title: Fitch Affirms Belgium's Credit Rating, Warns of High Debt Levels
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Fitch Ratings affirmed Belgium's credit rating and outlook while warning that the country's strengths are somewhat offset by its high levels of debt and political environment.

The credit ratings firm assigned Belgium an A+ sovereign debt rating and a stable outlook due to its diversified and wealthy economy, as well as its membership in the eurozone.

Belgium's public debt is rising and is among the highest in the A rating category, Fitch said. Debt is set to be nearly 110% of gross domestic product by the end of this year, compared with the A rating average of 60%.

The nation's deficit is expected to start rising again in 2029 due to income tax reduction and a further rise in debt interest expenses.

Belgium's structural reforms implemented this year and last should contain social spending, Fitch said. However, fiscal pressure from rising costs persist and the reform measures have sparked protests.

Growth in the country was weaker in the first half of this year than expected, causing Fitch to lower its growth forecast for the year to 0.7%. Private consumption has suffered from higher energy prices, while exports are starting to recover after years of underperformance.

data.title: Quantum Cyber Names Caplon CFO
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Quantum Cyber N.V. named David Caplon chief financial officer following the resignation of William Caragol on Friday.

Caplon succeeds William Caragol, who had notified the defense company on Friday that he was resigning. Caragol entered into a consulting agreement with the company and will receive a fee of $15,000 per month.

Caplon, who became CFO effective Friday, has been the company's controller since June 2026. He has also been corporate controller of CapForce, a financial technology company.

As part of his employment, Caplon will receive a base salary of $22,500 per month and will be eligible to receive a target annual cash bonus equal to 100% of his annual base salary.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: Corn basis steady-higher, soy basis steady-lower
data.description:
Basis bids for soybeans were steady to lower in the US Midwest on Friday, while corn basis bids were flat to higher, dealers said.

  • Dealers have been trying to incentivize farmers to sell their crops this week, as US futures prices have been under pressure and the completion of the harvest has kept producers busy.

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported on Friday that exporters sold 100,000 metric tons of soymeal to Spain for delivery in the 2026/27 marketing year.

  • Deforestation rules going into effect in the European Union in late December could steer soymeal export demand toward US supplies and, in turn, create more domestic demand for the oilseed in the US, analysts said.

  • CBOT January soybeans settled up 13-1/4 cents at $12.20-3/4 per bushel, bolstered by fresh export demand for soymeal and expectations of tightening US soybean inventories.

  • CBOT December corn ended down 4-1/2 cents at $4.34-1/2 per bushel, though the benchmark March contract stayed above a 4-1/2-month low set one day earlier.

data.title: TechCreate Group Ltd. Provides Update on NYSE American Delisting Proceedings
data.description:
TechCreate Group Ltd. (OTCMKTS: TCGLF) (“TechCreate” or the “Company”), a technology consultancy and advanced software solutions provider specializing in payment solutions, cybersecurity, and digital services, announced that the NYSE American Committee for Review (the “Committee”) has unanimously determined to affirm the decision of the NYSE American LLC (“NYSE American” or the “Exchange”) Listing Qualifications Panel (the “Panel”) with respect to the delisting of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares. Following its review, the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board”) has determined not to pursue any further challenge to the Committee’s decision.

The Committee’s written decision, dated November 9, 2026, follows a hearing held on October 22, 2026 and affirms the Panel’s August 20, 2026 opinion, which upheld the NYSE American Staff (“Staff”) determination to commence delisting proceedings. The proceedings stem from the one-day trading suspension of the Company’s securities ordered by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) and effective on February 2, 2026, the stated basis for which was potential manipulation of the Company’s securities through social media recommendations made by unknown persons.

In reaching its determination, the Board reviewed the sequence of the appeal proceedings and the Committee’s written decision, and considered the following:

  • No finding of wrongdoing. The Committee’s decision states that the Staff’s investigation into the manipulative trading of the Company’s securities did not result in a finding of wrongdoing on the part of the Company or any of its officers and directors.

  • Exchange discretion. The Committee determined that the NYSE American Company Guide (the “Company Guide”) gives the Staff discretion to delist a security regardless of whether the issuer complies with applicable listing standards. The Committee acknowledged the preventive measures the Company put forward, including voluntary surveillance, reporting and escalation procedures, and enhanced Board oversight, but did not consider them sufficient to continue the listing.

  • Focus on the business. The Board believes the Company’s time and resources are better directed to operating and growing the business, and to evaluating alternatives intended to protect the interests of shareholders.

Under Section 1206 of the Company Guide, the Committee’s decision may be called for review by the Exchange’s Board of Directors at the request of one or more of its directors. If the decision is not called for review, the Company will be notified that it represents the final action of the Exchange. If the decision is not called for review and the Company receives such notice, the Exchange is expected to proceed with delisting of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares. The Company’s securities continue to be quoted in the over-the-counter market under the symbol TCGLF.

About TechCreate Group Ltd.

TechCreate Group Ltd. is a Singapore-based payment software solutions provider. Founded in 2015, the Company delivers digital payment and infrastructure solutions to financial institutions, telecommunications companies, deposit insurers and enterprises. TechCreate’s offerings include real-time payment systems, digital banking platforms, API management, cybersecurity and cloud computing. Its proprietary Artificial Intelligence Real-Time Engine (AI-RTE) is designed to enable fast, secure and efficient payment processing. For more information, visit https://www.techcreate.com.sg/.

data.title: Ironman Announces Amendment to Convertible Debentures
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

LANGLEY, BC, November 20, 2026 – TheNewswire – Ironman International Ltd. (TSXV: IMI) (OTCQB: IMITF) ("Ironman" or the "Company") announces that it is seeking TSX Venture Exchange ("TSXV") acceptance for an extension of the maturity date and a reduction of the conversion price of the aggregate $500,000 principal amount of the secured convertible debentures ("Debentures") that were originally issued on November 22, 2022.

The Debentures are convertible into common shares of the Company (“Shares”) and mature on November 22, 2026. The Company is seeking approval of the TSXV to amend the Debentures (the “Replacement Debentures”) on maturity to reduce the conversion price of the Debentures from $0.10 to $0.05 per Share and extend the maturity date to November 30, 2026. The Debentures bear interest at a rate of 12.0% per annum, which has been paid in cash by the Company on a monthly basis. The Debentures have a remaining principal amount of an aggregate of $500,000.

The issuance of the Replacement Debentures remains subject to TSXV acceptance. The Company will issue a subsequent news release upon receipt of TSXV acceptance.

Related Party Transaction

Debentures having a principal amount of $225,000 are held by 599837 B.C. Ltd. (“599”), a company owned and controlled by Mike Irmen, director of the Company, and Debentures having a principal amount of $25,000 are held by Robert Scott, a director of the Company. As such, the Replacement Debentures issued to 599 and Mr. Scott will constitute a “related party transaction” pursuant to Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions (“MI 61-101”). The Company has relied on the exemptions from the valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements of MI 61-101 contained in sections 5.5(a) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101 on the basis that the Debentures do not exceed 25% of the fair market value of the Company’s market capitalization.

About Ironman International Ltd.

Established in 1999, Ironman International Ltd. is a leading North American provider of horizontal directional drilling and trenchless infrastructure services, operating 24/7 to support residential, commercial, industrial, and utility clients. The Company specializes in delivering cost-effective, low-impact underground installation solutions across a broad range of applications, including telecommunications, electrical, water and sewer, oil and gas, geothermal, and irrigation systems. With a modern fleet of specialized equipment and an experienced technical team, Ironman is capable of executing complex projects across diverse and challenging environments, including lakes, rivers, coastal and near-shore marine installations, rail corridors, roadways, and highways. The Company also provides complementary services designed to enhance efficiency, maintain safety standards, and ensure projects are completed on time and on budget. The common shares of Ironman International Ltd. are listed on the TSX Venture Exchange and trade under the symbol “IMI” and trade on the OTCQB Venture Market under the symbol “IMITF”.

data.title: Beta Fintech Withdraws Planned IPO
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Beta Fintech, a Hong Kong-based financial services provider, withdrew its planned initial public offering Friday.

The company had initially filed a foreign registration statement on form F-1 with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June 2025, and then again in February.

Beta Fintech requested the withdrawal of the February statement on Friday, and said the registration statement wasn't declared effective by the SEC.

The company said it plans to file a new registration statement for its IPO.

data.title: Fitch Affirms Belgium's Credit Rating, Warns of High Debt Levels
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Fitch Ratings affirmed Belgium's credit rating and outlook while warning that the country's strengths are somewhat offset by its high levels of debt and political environment.

The credit ratings firm assigned Belgium an A+ sovereign debt rating and a stable outlook due to its diversified and wealthy economy, as well as its membership in the eurozone.

Belgium's public debt is rising and is among the highest in the A rating category, Fitch said. Debt is set to be nearly 110% of gross domestic product by the end of this year, compared with the A rating average of 60%.

The nation's deficit is expected to start rising again in 2029 due to income tax reduction and a further rise in debt interest expenses.

Belgium's structural reforms implemented this year and last should contain social spending, Fitch said. However, fiscal pressure from rising costs persist and the reform measures have sparked protests.

Growth in the country was weaker in the first half of this year than expected, causing Fitch to lower its growth forecast for the year to 0.7%. Private consumption has suffered from higher energy prices, while exports are starting to recover after years of underperformance.
